subject: math

objective.text: Use different strategies to make 1 dollar or make change from 1 dollar.

explanations.title: 100 cents is 1 dollar
explanations.text: 100 cents is the same as 1 dollar. In a number sentence we can write 100 for the whole. We know the unit is cents.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (S: 100 cents is just shown as the number 100)

explanations.title: Count up to a dollar
explanations.text: To find how much more you need to make 100 cents, count up from what you have. Use friendly numbers, like tens. The arrow way shows the jumps.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (counting up with the arrow way)

explanations.title: Subtract from a dollar
explanations.text: You can also subtract from 100. 100 minus 30 is 70. Then take away the rest. Both ways find the missing part.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (S: You can subtract 35 from 100. 100 minus 30 is 70, and 70 minus 5 is 65)

explanations.title: What is change?
explanations.text: Change is the money you get back at the store. You pay with more money than the cost. The cashier keeps the cost. The leftover money is your change.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1 (what do you know about change)

explanations.title: Number bond for a dollar
explanations.text: A number bond for a dollar has 1 dollar, or 100 cents, as the whole. One part is the money you know. The other part is the missing money.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2 (number bond; the whole is $1, one part is 17 cents)

examples.title: 35 cents to a dollar
examples.text: You have a quarter and a dime. That is 35 cents. Add a nickel to make 40. Add a dime to make 50. Add 2 quarters to make 100. You need 65 cents more.

examples.title: 28 cents from a dollar
examples.text: You have 28 cents. Count up by dimes and then pennies: 38, 48, 58, 68, 78, 88, 98, 99, 100. 28 plus 72 makes 100. You have 72 cents left.

examples.title: 17 cents and the hidden coins
examples.text: One part is 17 cents. The whole is 1 dollar. 17 plus 83 makes 100. The hidden money is 83 cents.

examples.title: Candy and change
examples.text: You start with 1 dollar. You get 66 cents back as change. Count up from 66: 70, 75, 100. The candy costs 34 cents.
